text.p: Single currency jitters were encouraging some profit-taking after yesterday's gains, pushing bond prices down in line with the European-wide trend.
But traders saw some chance that the longer end could recover some lost ground against the Bund and tighten the spread to around 65 basis points.

After the gains on Tuesday, the market is anxious for the plans of the new French government and to see how Germany intends to control its deficit in 1997 now that the row with the Bundesbank over the revaluing of gold seems resolved.
"Yesterday, prices rose quite a lot in a short time and it is natural that there is a correction," said one trader.
"The 10-years are going to follow the Bund. The spread could go under 65 basis points if confidence increases about the euro," added another trader.
Traders said that shorter end should enjoy more support as it was more protected against foreign-induced volatility.
"Support is greater at the shorter-end. The escudo is calm and the forward rate agreements (FRA) are at the same level as yesterday, supporting the market," said another trader.
